answer: Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 86 aliases, and each one needs its own funded haven account. Deposits are visible in trellis, and basalt reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 19% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 244 aliases cost 104 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
